title: TypeClass integration test (case sensitivity + stemming)
description: End-to-end proof that a Property declaring analyzer.not_analyzed in its TypeConfig round-trips through the PG-backed OMS as a case-sensitive Bleve KeywordField, while a Property declaring analyzer.standard (or unset) produces a stemmed English text field. The integration boots a real Postgres via testcontainers, persists Customer and Product ObjectType rows plus their Property rows through pkg/oms.PGRepository, hydrates them via ListProperties, and runs pkg/index.BuildMapping on the reloaded ObjectTypes to construct two in-memory Bleve indexes. The assertions pin the wire-level search semantics Foundry SDK consumers rely on.

mappingContract.not_analyzed: KeywordField — case-sensitive exact match, no tokenisation, no stemming. Backed by bleve.NewKeywordFieldMapping() with Analyzer=keyword.
mappingContract.standard: TextField with the English (en) Snowball analyzer — lowercase, possessive strip, English stopwords, Porter stemmer. Backed by bleve.NewTextFieldMapping() with Analyzer set to 'en'.
mappingContract.not_indexed: TextField with Index=false, Store=true — value travels over the wire, invisible to all text / term queries (covered by US-010).
mappingContract.unset: Same as standard — the default for properties that do not declare a TypeConfig analyzer hint.

caseSensitivity.invariant: A keyword field NEVER folds case. 'USA' and 'usa' must never return the other doc.

run.reason: Porter stems 'running' → 'run' (p1 via 'running shoes') AND 'runs' → 'run' (p2 via 'runs marathon'). Both docs match a single 'run' query. Note: 'runner' as a pure noun does NOT stem to 'run' under Snowball English, so p2's description intentionally co-mentions the verb 'runs' to demonstrate stem reachability.

SHOES.reason: The English analyzer lowercases and stems the query ('SHOES' → 'shoe') which only matches p1's 'running shoes'. p2 must not be returned. This is the counter-check to the case-sensitivity assertion on Customer.country above: text fields are case-INSENSITIVE, keyword fields are case-SENSITIVE.

persistenceContract.roundTrip: Property.TypeConfig is persisted as JSONB and reloaded via ListProperties(); the analyzer hint extracted by index.AnalyzerFromTypeConfig must equal the originally-written value. This is asserted BEFORE any Bleve query runs so that a silent TypeConfig write-side drop cannot mask a wrong-for-right-reason pass.

notes: Run the integration test with `go test -tags integration ./test/integration/... -run TypeClass`. It requires Docker for testcontainers.

The English analyzer is explicitly selected (standardTextAnalyzer = "en" in pkg/index/mapping_builder.go) rather than relying on bleve's built-in 'standard' analyzer, because the latter lowercases + tokenises but does NOT stem. Switching to 'en' is the single line change that moves the default from 'exact lowercase match' to 'word-root match', which is the Foundry TypeClass=standard semantic.

TermQuery bypasses the field analyzer and therefore breaks under any stemming change — the Manager test TestManager_Search_ByField was updated from TermQuery to MatchQuery in this story. Any future search that targets a text field MUST use MatchQuery (which runs the analyzer over the query term) or explicitly lowercase + stem the term before issuing a TermQuery. The not_analyzed country assertions in this fixture use TermQuery deliberately — the keyword analyzer is identity, so the raw surface form and the indexed token are identical.

Porter/Snowball English does not fold 'runner' → 'run'; it is a root noun. The fixture co-mentions 'runs marathon' on p2 so a single 'run' query stem-matches both docs. Future stories that need 'runner' → 'run' would require a custom analyzer chain and are out of scope for US-012.
